To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Germans are unable to estimate their position in the income-distribution of their country; they know little about income inequality and the factors that determine it; they are aware that they are ignorant; they would prefer more redistribution; and they do not change their preferences after being provided with information.

Germans are unaware of their income position and the degree of income inequality, they prefer more redistribution and that this preference does not change when they learn more about the income distribution.
(1) Germans do not know much and are well aware of it, (2) they prefer more redistribution than what they think is the case, and (3) providing accurate information does not change their preference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what Germans think and know and what they do with their knowledge.
the relationship between knowledge and preferences for redistribution.
how citizens think about income distribution and how they respond to information about the income structure in their society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Germans are ignorant, but not necessarily misinformed about their own position in society, and they do not know much more about the social structure.
German public opinion is in favor of more income redistribution than the current system provides.
Germans do not care much about the distribution of income and wealth, do not know much and are not interested in learning more.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Germans are not aware of the income distribution, but they do care about it.
Germans are not aware that they are well-off and they do not know how unequal their society is.
Germans know little about their own income position, about income inequality in their country and about the tax-transfer system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the public does not have a good understanding of the facts about income inequality, but this does not prevent people from having a well-defined and stable opinion about the desirability of more redistribution.
Germans are well informed about income distribution, but they do not use this information to inform their policy preferences.
people do not like inequality and would like to live in a more egalitarian world, even though they are not aware of the true extent to which inequality exists.
